newsitem.title: LATVIA: WATERWAYS ON PUBLIC OFFER IN JUNE.
newsitem.headline: WATERWAYS ON PUBLIC OFFER IN JUNE.

text.p: The Latvian Privatisation Agency (LPA) said on Wednesday that Latvia's Waterways (Udensceli), a dredging and marine repair company, will be on public offer from June 2 till June 27.
"I hope the high price the controlling stake owner paid for its share will motivate it to recoup the investment," Janis Naglis, LPA general director, told a news conference.
The public offer will include 22.5 percent of the Waterways stock of 650,000 shares or 166,500 shares and 20 percent will be sold to the employees.
Waterways controling stake, 51 percent or 331,500 shares, is held by the Swiss owned Vudisona Terminals company, active in oil transit.
Vudisona Terminals paid 1.47 million lats for its stake.
The strategic investor has to invest one million lats within three years, according to the sell-off rules.
Waterways posted 204,174 lats of losses in 1996 on net turnover of 1.34 million lats. Its balance sheet total was 390,930 lats.
The company's main market is the Baltic Sea region, with 50 percent of its operations in Estonia and Lithuania and some 25 percent in Sweden and Finland.
Apart from dredging operations and repair work, it also operates seven vessels, currently registered as the property of the former Soviet Union. The owenership issue has yet to be clarified.
